newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala mulls shift to lethal injection.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala mulls shift to lethal injection.

text.p: Weeks after Guatemala's media was flooded with images of a botched firing squad execution, Congress is studying a bill that would change the method to lethal injection, an official said on Wednesday.

"The bill that would change execution from firing squad to lethal injection came about as a consequence of the recent firing squad," said Carlos Alarcon Monsanto, assistant to the president of Congress, who presented the law.

The Sept. 13 execution of the two men, convicted of raping and murdering a 4-year-old girl, enjoyed overwhelming popular support among Guatemalans, who are frustrated with high crime rates and ineffective courts.

But the method of execution sparked controversy after children were exposed to graphic newspaper and television coverage, including a coup de grace pistol shot to the heads of each convict after a volley from the firing squad failed to kill them.
A congressional committee is studying the law which will go to the full Congress for debate within two months, said Alarcon.
